---
title: "SEPIA"
subtitle: "Systematic Evaluation of Pigmentation In Archaic hominins"
---

**SEPIA** — *Systematic Evaluation of Pigmentation In Archaic hominins* — asks what the genetics of pigmentation (skin, hair, and eye colour) can, and cannot, tell us about Neanderthals and Denisovans, and how they compare to present-day human variation. The recurring public question is *"what did archaic humans look like?"* SEPIA asks how much their ancient DNA can actually answer — and stays explicit about where the data runs out.

## The headline result

Where the archaic hominins fall relative to modern humans depends entirely on *which* pigmentation variants you look at. We build a PCA on modern human genomes and project the archaics onto it in three ways — the whole genome, whole pigmentation-*gene* regions, and a hand-picked panel of pigmentation-associated SNPs. The whole genome and the pigmentation genes give the **same** answer: the archaics sit as a divergent outgroup, exactly as their deep ancestry predicts. Only the **ascertained SNP panel** places them "with Africans" — and that is a footprint of **selection and ascertainment**, not ancestry: the panel is enriched for the derived, out-of-Africa light-skin alleles that archaics (like the earliest-splitting African lineages) simply never carried.

So the one-line takeaway is **genes track ancestry; hand-picked SNPs track selection** — a caution for anyone reading a pigmentation-SNP panel as if it described who is related to whom. The full logic, figures, and method are in the [projection workbook](archaic_projection.qmd).

## The approach

SEPIA is a **QC-first re-analysis**. It continues the honors thesis **PAINT** (Lily Heald, 2026) but rebuilds the analysis from clearly-traced inputs, because archaic DNA is patchy and shallow and pigmentation genes don't behave like ancestry markers. Every figure is regenerated from a documented pipeline so its provenance is auditable, and known pitfalls — genome-build mismatches, degenerate PCAs, imputation artefacts — are checked rather than assumed away. The work runs as a phased plan: trace inputs → one verified genome build → positive controls → sample QC → the pigmentation analyses → reproducible infrastructure → writing.

The archaic set is chosen for reliability, not count. SEPIA genotypes the **9 genomes** — 5 high-coverage (Altai/Denisova 5, Vindija 33.19, Denisova 3, Chagyrskaya 8, Denisova 25) plus 4 low-coverage (Les Cottés, Denisova 11, Goyet, Mezmaiskaya 1) — that can contribute trustworthy calls at the panel, and deliberately excludes exome-only, redundant, and ultra-low-coverage genomes by [documented inclusion criteria](plan/papers/SAMPLE_INCLUSION.html).

- [Project plan & roadmap](plan/sepia-plan.html) — the phased plan, bug fixes, and the Q1–Q10 QC checks.
- [Changelog & decision log](plan/changelog.html) — dated record of what's been done, found, and decided.

## Status

- **v1 — honors thesis (PAINT, 2026, Lily Heald).** Framed the feasibility question: how complete and deep is archaic sequencing at pigmentation loci, and where do archaic samples fall relative to modern humans?
- **In progress — SEPIA.** Rebuilding on clearly-traced data: a completed 159-genome modern reference, a harmonised genome build, genotype-likelihood handling for low-coverage genomes, the extended SNP surface, and the redone principal-component projections — plus a *Trends in Genetics* review.

## What the work finds (so far)

Archaic sequencing is uneven and often shallow, and missing data is non-random (older samples have more of it). On their own, ascertained pigmentation SNPs don't separate populations the way the whole genome does — and where they *do* deviate reflects selection history, not ancestry. Confident, species-wide claims about archaic pigmentation are not well supported; the contribution is an honest map of what the genetics does and doesn't show.

## Data & provenance

- **Simons Genome Diversity Project (SGDP)** — modern human reference genomes.
- **Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology (MPI-EVA)** — archaic Neanderthal and Denisovan genomes.
- **NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog**, plus forensic (HIrisPlex-S) and gene-network sources — pigmentation-associated variants.
- **NASA Earth Observations** — UV-index climatology.

Per-file provenance — and where the large, cluster-only data live — is documented in [`data/README.md`](https://github.com/lasisilab/sepia/blob/main/data/README.md); per-genome sources are in the [provenance tables](plan/papers/REFERENCES.html).
